audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-dominant, final syllable of the phonological word) rests on the only full phonological description of this variety, a 2020 UNAM MA thesis of xxv+389 pp classified by Glottolog as a phonology, and the quotation is verbatim at §3.3 p.107 and §6.2.1.1 p.221 of the PDF downloaded now. The author's 2024 open-access LangSci chapter independently restates obligatory, culminative, right-edge stress on the root+suffix domain with enclitics excluded, so nothing suggests a reclassify; the record previously held no file and carries an empty grade/cite/loc, so the action is to attach the now-held PDF (cite + locator p.107/p.221) and set the strength of the evidence. One nuance worth carrying into the domain field if it is ever coded: the stress domain is the phonological word (root + comitative suffix, compounds = last stem); syllabic enclitics are unstressed and outside it, and the description is i

sources.citation: Nakamoto 2020, Tonologia mazateca: San Bartolome Ayautla, MA thesis UNAM, hdl 20.500.14330/TES01000801819, full PDF secs. 3.3 and 6.2.1.1
sources.quote: El mazateco tiene acento fijo en la última sílaba de la palabra fonológica ... Incluso en los préstamos, el acento siempre cae en la sílaba final (§4.4.4). ... los prefijos silábicos no afectan la posición del acento.

sources.quote: 'El mazateco tiene acento fijo en la última sílaba de la palabra fonológica' (p.107); loans and prefixed forms keep final stress, comitative suffix -ko13 takes the stress, compounds stress the last stem, syllabic enclitics never stressed (pp.220-222); no secondary stress.

sources.quote: 'Stress in Ayautla Mazatec is phonetically semi-long with an increased intensity, and is obligatory, culminative and predictably assigned on the right edge (or the end) of the stress domain' -- domain = verb root plus comitative suffix (positions 19-20); enclitics after position 20 do not shift the stress; independent pronouns carry their own stress.
sources.locator: §3.8 'Stress assignment (19-20, 15-20)', chapter-PDF pp. xx-xxi (PDF pages 20-21; published pagination ~250-251)
